title: The Lid in the Wrong Bin
transcript: At a public recycling station, attendants kept finding drink cups in the paper bin. The cups looked like cardboard, but their inner lining meant the local processor could not recycle them with ordinary paper. A volunteer watched the station one afternoon and noticed that people usually glanced at the pictures and ignored the printed list. The station replaced a general recycling symbol with a large photo of a familiar takeaway cup on the waste bin. A week later, attendants found fewer cups mixed with paper. Plastic lids still turned up in the wrong bin, so the team decided to test separate pictures for cups and lids.

questions.prompt: What did the volunteer notice about how people used the signs?
options: They read the list when the bins were nearly full.
They compared the written instructions on several bins.
They relied mainly on the colors of the bins.
They looked at the pictures and generally skipped the text.
questions.answer: They looked at the pictures and generally skipped the text.
questions.explanation: 志愿者发现，人们通常扫一眼图片，很少看印出的清单。

questions.prompt: What did the results suggest about the new sign?
options: It was more effective for lids than for cups.
It helped people sort cups and lids equally well.
It reduced mistakes with cups while leaving a problem with lids.
It reduced mistakes only when attendants were present.
questions.answer: It reduced mistakes with cups while leaving a problem with lids.
questions.explanation: 纸类箱中的杯子少了，但塑料杯盖仍会被投错。
